# Infinitude — two independent proofs that primes never run out

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean

Euclid's argument using the combined cycle plus one; and a counting argument showing a fixed finite set of wheels cannot build enough square-free parts for every number.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Euclid, Elements, Book IX, Proposition 20 (D. E. Joyce's edition)](https://mathcs.clarku.edu/~djoyce/elements/bookIX/propIX20.html) — the classical argument behind the first proof
- [Number of Primes is Infinite, Proof 6 (ProofWiki)](https://www.proofwiki.org/wiki/Number_of_Primes_is_Infinite/Proof_6) — the square-times-squarefree counting argument behind the second proof

## Claims

<a id="euclid_primes_unbounded"></a>
### `euclid_primes_unbounded`

Above every bound there is a prime (Euclid, via the combined cycle plus one).

```lean
/-- **Euclid, via the combined cycle.** Above every bound there is a prime:
the combined cycle of all primes below the bound, plus one, has a prime
factor that cannot be below the bound. -/
def euclid_primes_unbounded : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : Nat, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ limit ≤ p
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Infinitude.euclid_primes_unbounded_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Infinitude.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Infinitude.lean)

<a id="squarefree_counting_no_finite_supply"></a>
### `squarefree_counting_no_finite_supply`

No bound has all primes below it (square-free counting).

```lean
/-- **No finite supply of wheels, by counting.** For no bound are all primes
below it: if they were, every number would be a square times a divisor of the
fixed combined cycle, and there are too few such pairs to cover every number
up to a large enough ceiling. -/
def squarefree_counting_no_finite_supply : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : Nat, ¬ ∀ p, p.Prime → p < limit
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.Infinitude.squarefree_counting_no_finite_supply_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/Infinitude.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Infinitude.lean)
